blocks.text: 完成订晚餐、约理发这类事情很费时间。实时电话对话节奏很快，很少按剧本走。电话那头的人几乎什么话都可能说，还常常说到一半就改口——而人们往往靠细微的语气变化来判断该谁开口。停顿多出半秒，听起来就像电话断了；抢话太早，又会变成两个人同时说话。要借助 AI 在电话里得体地完成这些事，我们必须让高质量的语音理解、上下文推理和语音合成在同一个低延迟系统里协同工作。

inlines.text: 对话架构的三代演进

blocks.text: 过去十年间，支撑这些通话的技术栈经历了三个截然不同的阶段，从定制的神经网络流水线走向使用 Gemini 的统一架构。

inlines.text: 过去十年间，支撑这些通话的技术栈经历了三个截然不同的阶段，从定制的神经网络流水线走向使用 Gemini 的统一架构。

blocks.text: 1. 大语言模型之前的封闭领域模型

inlines.text: 1. 大语言模型之前的封闭领域模型

blocks.text: 早在现代语言模型出现之前，甚至早在 transformer 被发明出来之前，我们就已经启动了 Google Duplex 的研发工作。在早期阶段，为了确保商家和用户都能获得良好体验，我们把 Duplex 限制在较窄的领域内，并基于匿名化的特定任务电话对话训练定制的循环神经网络模型。由于没有预训练的世界知识，我们只能教会模型如何高效处理每一种具体任务。在实践中，这意味着每种任务类型都依赖大量训练数据——比如要理解餐厅预订与查询节假日营业时间这两种截然不同的固定流程——才能确保系统可靠地应对特定领域的逻辑。

blocks.text: 2. 早期生成式模型与混合架构

inlines.text: 2. 早期生成式模型与混合架构

blocks.text: 随着开放域基础模型的出现，Google Duplex 开始将其投入生产环境。例如，2022 年 Duplex 在实时通话中使用了 LaMDA。这些预训练模型简化了语义理解和常识推理，让系统能够应对意料之外的对话转折和跑题，同时仍能紧扣上下文，像标准的餐厅预订那样推进对话。

blocks.text: 不过，这些早期生成式模型的可预测性不如今天，有时速度也更慢，因此我们构建了混合架构：用生成式模型负责灵活措辞，用确定性的状态跟踪和严格的策略护栏来兜底。这有助于确保用户和商家都能获得良好体验。

blocks.text: 3. 无边界任务与 Gemini 集成

inlines.text: 3. 无边界任务与 Gemini 集成

blocks.text: 随着基础模型不断进步，我们彻底取消了固定垂直领域的限制，转而用自由文本的任务描述来提示系统。这样一来，模型只需一段提示词就能定义任务，系统便能泛化到新的任务类型和细节（比如要求靠窗座位，或需要放婴儿车的额外空间）以及新的商家类别，无需从零构建独立的对话模型。

网页并不包含捕捉与忙碌商家通话如何展开所需的全部数据。近十年面向目标通话的经验，帮助我们的架构掌握语用规范，而且从通话开始之前就已介入。在实践中，这意味着根据过往对话的历史上下文，将自由文本任务与商家匹配（例如知道某家商户周末不接待大型团体预订），从而预判任务能否成功。在通话过程中，这有助于模型判断在某一时刻问什么才合理、如何读懂礼貌的间接拒绝，以及如何让通话简短高效。
嘈杂环境下的亚秒级延迟：
通话经由压缩的电话线路传输，背景中充斥着厨房里的锅碗碰撞声、意式咖啡机的轰鸣、街道噪音和旁人交谈。我们的技术栈针对低延迟流式推理做了调优，让回复以自然的节奏送达。定制的声学模型和对话节奏模型协助核心 AI 系统处理背景噪音和停顿、在预期时停止说话等。

blocks.text: 为通话两端而设计

inlines.text: 为通话两端而设计

blocks.text: Duplex 既要服务好接听电话的商家，也要服务好用户。这一原则塑造了若干设计选择：

inlines.text: Duplex 既要服务好接听电话的商家，也要服务好用户。这一原则塑造了若干设计选择：
明确披露。
每通电话开头都会清楚说明这是 AI 智能体——具体来说，是来自 Google 的自动系统在呼叫。
商家保有控制权。
商家可以在 Google Business Profile 设置中
选择退出
自动来电，也可以在通话中直接说“请不要再打给我的商家”。
无需设置，零适配。
Duplex 走的是商家本来就在接听的电话线路：不用安装软件，不用维护预订系统，也不用培训员工。接电话的人可以像对待任何顾客一样处理这通电话，哪怕正赶上高峰期、柜台前排着队。
一次对话，多处受益。
一通电话里收集到的信息可以回答之后的许多问题，商家不必反复被问同样的事。例如，Google 地图可以展示 Duplex 收集到的商家信息，比如欢乐时光特惠、露天座位、是否宠物友好、停车小贴士，甚至每周一次的 trivia 之夜。

blocks.text: 结语

inlines.text: 结语

blocks.text: 许多日常琐事、本地服务和紧急任务，仍然需要直接与人交谈才能可靠地协调细节。通过把 Duplex 的能力集成到 Gemini App 的 Tasks 中，我们又向打通这一环迈出了一步。自然语音交互成为一种无缝集成的交互方式，当在线 API 或预订表单这类结构化数字渠道不存在时，智能体随时可以启用它。借助我们最新的 Gemini 4 模型——包括 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 和 Gemini 4 Neon——Gemini 中的 Tasks 现在可以支持更全面的工作流，比如分析水电费账单、通过 Agent Payments Protocol 安全处理交易，以及通过电子邮件和富通信服务（RCS）与用户协调。借助这些能力，我们正把这项研究带入下一代 AI 助手。

blocks.text: Completing tasks like making dinner reservations or booking a hair appointment is time consuming. Live phone conversations move fast and rarely follow a script. The person on the other end can say almost anything, often revising their thoughts mid-sentence – and people often rely on subtle tone changes to indicate whose turn it is to speak. Pause half a second too long, and it sounds like the call dropped; speak too soon, and you end up talking over each other. Leveraging AI to complete these tasks respectfully over the phone required us to consider high quality speech understanding, contextual reasoning, and speech synthesis working together in a single, low-latency system.

blocks.text: We introduced Google Duplex nearly a decade ago to help address this challenge. Propelled by advances in foundation models, the Duplex architecture has evolved to power autonomous task completion across many core products, such as Google Search and Maps. This week, we launched Duplex in Tasks in Gemini App, a personal AI collaborator that can help coordinate real-world chores, like calling businesses for you and handling real-world requests on behalf of the user. In this post, we look back at the decade-long architectural evolution that made this possible — moving from early, closed-domain models to a unified stack built entirely with Gemini.

blocks.text: 1. Pre-LLM closed-domain models

inlines.text: 1. Pre-LLM closed-domain models

blocks.text: We started work on Google Duplex before modern language models and even before the transformer itself was invented. In these early days, to ensure businesses and users had a great experience, we constrained Duplex to narrow domains and trained custom recurrent neural network models on anonymized, task-specific phone conversations. Without pre-trained world knowledge, we taught our models how to handle every specific type of task efficiently. In practice, this meant relying on extensive training data for each task type — such as interpreting the rigid flow of restaurant booking versus checking holiday hours — to ensure the system could reliably navigate domain-specific logic.

blocks.text: 2. Early generative models and hybrid stacks

inlines.text: 2. Early generative models and hybrid stacks

blocks.text: Google Duplex started employing open domain foundation models in production as they emerged. For example, in 2022 Duplex used LaMDA in live calls. These pre-trained models simplified comprehension and common-sense reasoning, allowing the system to handle unexpected conversational turns and tangents, while remaining grounded in the context like a standard restaurant booking.

blocks.text: However, these early generative models were less predictable and sometimes slower than today's, so we built hybrid stacks that paired generative models for flexible phrasing with deterministic state tracking and strict policy guardrails. This helped ensure that both users and businesses had a great experience.

blocks.text: 3. Unbounded tasks and Gemini integration

inlines.text: 3. Unbounded tasks and Gemini integration

blocks.text: As foundation models advanced, we removed the constraint of fixed verticals entirely by shifting to prompting the system with free-text task descriptions. This allowed models to define a task simply via a prompt, enabling the system to generalize to new task types and nuances (like asking for window seating or extra space for a stroller) and new business categories, without building separate dialogue models from scratch.

blocks.text: Technical hurdles in live telephony

inlines.text: Technical hurdles in live telephony

blocks.text: Even with frontier models, live telephony poses hurdles that pre-training on standard datasets like the web alone doesn't solve:

inlines.text: Even with frontier models, live telephony poses hurdles that pre-training on standard datasets like the web alone doesn't solve:
Pragmatic grounding for pre-call and conversational context, and real-world intent understanding:

The web doesn’t have all the data needed to capture how calls unfold with busy merchants. Nearly a decade of experience with goal-directed calls helps our stack grasp pragmatic norms, starting even before the call. In practice, this means matching a free-text task with a business based on the historical context of past conversations (e.g., knowing a specific vendor doesn't take reservations for large groups over the weekend) to predict whether a task will work. During the call, this helps the model determine what makes sense to ask at a given moment, how to read polite indirect refusals, and how to keep calls brief and effective.
Sub-second latency in noisy acoustic setups:

Calls run over compressed phone lines against loud backdrops like clattering in kitchens, espresso machines, street noise, and side chatter. Our stack is tuned for low-latency streaming inference so replies land at a natural cadence. Custom acoustic and conversation cadence models assist the core AI system with handling background noise and pauses, stop talking when expected, etc.

blocks.text: Designing for both ends of the line

inlines.text: Designing for both ends of the line

blocks.text: Duplex has to work just as well for the business answering the phone as it does for the user. That principle shaped several design choices:

inlines.text: Duplex has to work just as well for the business answering the phone as it does for the user. That principle shaped several design choices:
Clear disclosure.
Every call opens by clearly disclosing that it’s an AI agent — specifically, an automated system calling from Google.
Businesses stay in control.
Merchants can
opt out
of automated calls in their Google Business Profile settings, or simply say “Please stop calling my business” during a call.
No setup and zero adaptation.

Duplex works through the phone a business already answers: no software to install, no booking system to maintain and no staff to train. Whoever answers can handle the call the way they would with any customer, even mid-rush with a line at the counter.
One conversation, many insights.

Details gathered on one call can answer many later questions, so a business isn’t asked the same thing over and over. For example, Google Maps can show details that Duplex gathers about businesses, like happy hour specials, patio seating, pet-friendliness, a parking tip or even a weekly trivia night.

blocks.text: Conclusion

inlines.text: Conclusion

blocks.text: Many daily errands, local services, and urgent tasks still require speaking directly with another person to coordinate details reliably. By integrating Duplex’s capabilities into Tasks in Gemini App, we are taking another step toward closing this loop. Natural voice interaction becomes a seamlessly integrated modality that the agent can deploy whenever structured digital channels like online APIs or booking forms don't exist. Using our newest Gemini 4 models — including Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon — Tasks in Gemini can now support more comprehensive workflows like analyzing utility bills, processing transactions securely via the Agent Payments Protocol, and coordinating with users over email and Rich Communication Services (RCS). Through these capabilities, we are bringing this research into the next generation of AI assistance.
